label: Midterm review
title: From Euclid to finite fields
description: Cumulative practice through finite-fields Lecture 2: integers, continued fractions, congruences, arithmetic functions, valuations, primes, bases, and quadratic extensions. Two optional enrichment problems follow.
details: 16 core problems + 2 optional · 160 practice points · 5–7 hours

label: Problem Set 1
title: Euclid and the architecture of the integers
description: Divisibility, greatest common divisors, Bézout identities, prime factorization, and the infinitude of primes.

label: Week 2
title: Division, primes, and finite continued fractions
description: Turn Euclidean calculations, a sieve, and finite continued fractions into proofs. Test divisibility claims with counterexamples.

label: Problem Set 3
title: Totients, divisor sums, and exact periods
description: Extended Euclid and Euler's theorem lead into multiplicative functions, Möbius inversion, necklace counts, and squarefree integers.

label: Problem Set 4 · Optional enrichment
title: Orders, interpolation, and Fourier inversion
description: Invert counts on posets, subsets, and partitions, then recover polynomial coefficients at roots of unity and explore cyclic convolution.

label: Topic problem set
title: Multiplicative functions
description: Prime-power values, divisor functions, totients, convolution, Möbius cancellation, and counting applications.

label: Topic problem set
title: Valuations, primes, and p-adic distance
description: Factorial and binomial valuations, Chebyshev growth bounds, and a first introduction to p-adic distance, the ultrametric inequality, and convergence.

label: Weekly quiz collection
title: Ten checkpoints from Euclid to primes
description: Short, self-contained quizzes following the course sequence, with space to write calculations and proofs.
